(a) A TOKEN LEDGER: for named tasks — capture one requirement with its thread; orient on a design; judge one levied requirement — the calls made and the characters returned per call, summed per task. Characters are the recorded proxy for tokens, stated as such.
(b) LATENCY per tool on RELEASE builds against real designs (reflow2's own, ~5,900 nodes, and a small one), continuing the discipline of its four recorded wins and con:loop-status-after-a-write-answers-under-one-second.
(c) BUDGETS for both, written before any optimisation, recorded as Constraints, and re-measured each release so a regression is caught.
